stories.title: Equity Residential and AvalonBay: Inside the $71B Mega Multifamily Merger
stories.excerpt: On May 21, shortly before Memorial Day weekend, participants in public real estate markets awoke to a truly remarkable headline. AvalonBay Communities, the owner of 98,000 apartments and with a market capitalization of $25 billion, would be merging with Equity Residential, one of the oldest real estate investment trusts (REITs) in America, holding 85,000 apartments and $20.5 billion assets under management. “The initial reaction was, ‘Holy cow, two of the largest, most storied apartment REIT companies nationally are choosing to merge,’” said Allan Swaringen, president and CEO of JLL Income Property Trust, a REIT. “These are the two biggest gorillas in the multifamily marketplace who decided to come together. It’s a true merger of equals.” With a total enterprise value of roughly $71 billion, the deal marks the single largest public REIT merger ever, dwarfing the 2022 deal between Prologis and Duke Realty valued at $26 billion. The two apartment firms announced in late July their new company will be called Vivmark Residential. Once the all-stock merger is complete later this year, this new multifamily behemoth will own more than 180,000 rental apartments across more than 600 communities in the U.S. — mainly in the largest coastal cities — plus another 10,800 apartments and $4.4 billion under construction across 32 communities, of which 50 percent will hold an affordable or mixed-income component, the firms noted in a shared release. “My first reaction is they should’ve done it a few years ago. It’s a very natural merger,” said Matt Frankel, a stock market analyst at the Motley Fool, who noted that roughly 95 percent of Equity Residential and AvalonBay’s businesses operate out of the same markets, mainly New York, San Francisco, Boston and Washington, D.C. Equity is headquartered out of Chicago, while AvalonBay calls Arlington, Va., home. “This would be like if Visa or Mastercard were allowed to merge. bullets: AvalonBay (98K units, $25B market cap) merges Equity Residential (85K units, $20.5B AUM)
Combined enterprise value ~$71B; largest public REIT merger ever
Creates dominant 183K-unit platform with consolidated market power and capital deployment scale
stories.summary: AvalonBay Communities and Equity Residential announced a merger of equals with enterprise value around $71 billion, combining 98,000 and 85,000 apartments respectively. The deal creates the industry's largest consolidated multifamily REIT by unit count and capital base. This represents the largest public REIT merger in history, surpassing 2022's Prologis-Duke Realty transaction.
stories.impact: Consolidation at this scale reshapes competitive dynamics across major markets and signals confidence in multifamily fundamentals despite recent cap-rate pressures. The merged entity's enhanced balance sheet and unit density enable faster land acquisition and development execution in high-barrier-to-entry markets, potentially accelerating supply in supply-constrained metros and intensifying competition for best-in-class development sites for younger entrants like TCR.

stories.title: Sunday Summary: Seven. Hundred. Fifty. Billion.
stories.excerpt: Three-quarters of a trillion dollars can buy you pretty much anything you want. If you took the gross national product of Chile, and added the GNP of Colombia, you’d still have more than $100 billion left — and that can also get you pretty much anything in the known world. Well, J.P. Morgan Chase has decided to use that ungodly amount of lucre to invest it in a roof over one’s head. On Monday, the bank announced an unprecedented push to build $750 billion worth of housing over the next nine years with the goal of increasing both supply and homeownership nationwide. (Oh, yeah — Commercial Observer broke the story.) “We’re focused on helping more people access quality housing they can afford,” said Michelle Herrick, the bank’s head of commercial real estate. “And we’re working across the real estate community, local governments and nonprofits to scale housing solutions throughout the U.S.” J.P. Morgan’s approach will be to focus on expanding financing through debt, equity and grants, with a target of creating 1 million units of affordable housing. They’re hoping to aid 500,000 customers, of which they’re anticipating 200,000 will be first-time buyers. Of course, the timing of this is opportune. Back in May, CO reported that construction starts on multifamily projects throughout the U.S. for the first quarter of this year hadn’t been this low since 2011. But a few companies have been trying to meet the demand — at least in certain regions. In New York, for example, LMXD and Bedrock Real Estate Partners are building a 560-unit mixed-income development in Astoria. In Florida, Ultimate Equity just shelled out $32 million for a 69-unit townhome community in Hollywood. Krea USA is mid-construction on a 385-unit development called Le Parc at Lauderhill in Lauderhill, Fla. And Harbor Group International bought a zoo — actually, make that HGI bought a garden-style apartment complex near Zoo Miami. bullets: JPMorgan Chase commits $750B housing investment over 9 years
Target: 1M affordable units; 500K customer impact; debt, equity, grants structure
Unprecedented capital influx directly addresses supply and affordability at national scale
stories.summary: J.P. Morgan Chase announced a $750 billion housing investment initiative over nine years targeting 1 million affordable housing units and 500,000 customer impact. The bank will deploy capital via debt financing, equity, and grants, working with developers, local governments, and nonprofits. The announcement positions the bank as a systemic capital provider for affordable housing solutions nationwide.
stories.impact: This mega-commitment signals mega-bank conviction in housing scarcity and affordability as a structural problem requiring institutional capital. For multifamily developers, it creates a new primary lender/partner pathway for affordable and workforce projects, likely with better terms and longer hold horizons than traditional CMBS or bridge lenders. Expect easier acquisition financing and construction capital for mixed-income and 60–80% AMI products, widening the addressable pipeline for developers in gateway and secondary markets with affordable mandates.

stories.title: Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway
stories.excerpt: Colliers SVP Seth Hecht has secured a 10-year, 13,815-square-foot lease renewal for architecture firm Selldorf Architects at 860 Broadway. Hecht represented Gordon Property Group in completing the long-term renewal transaction. Selldorf Architects was represented by Erik Schmall and Scott Weiss of Savills. Led by internationally acclaimed architect Annabelle Selldorf, the firm has called 860 Broadway home for the past two decades. “860 Broadway is one of Manhattan’s iconic office buildings, and its location continues to make it a highly desirable destination for creative and innovative companies,” said Hecht. “When a firm as globally respected as Selldorf Architects commits to another decade in the building, it speaks to both the property’s enduring appeal and the long-term strength of this market.” In addition to Selldorf Architects, current 860 Broadway tenants include Industrious, Valon and retail tenant Uniqlo. Hecht is also representing Gordon Property Group in leasing three additional Manhattan office properties. The post Selldorf Architects Signs Long-Term Renewal at 860 Broadway appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Selldorf Architects renews 13,815 SF at Manhattan office icon 860 Broadway for 10 years
Two-decade tenant commitment signals office market durability in creative sector
Mixed-use building with Industrious, Valon, Uniqlo; strong leasing momentum
stories.summary: Architecture firm Selldorf Architects renewed its 13,815-square-foot lease at 860 Broadway in Manhattan for 10 years, representing a two-decade tenure. The long-term renewal by a globally respected design firm underscores the building's enduring appeal and signals continued demand from creative tenants.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Office leasing strength in creative buildings does not drive residential demand or inform apartment supply/demand dynamics; it reflects sector-specific real estate health, not housing market signals.

stories.title: Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation
stories.excerpt: Advertising agency Innocean USA has signed a new 101,000-square-foot office lease at Hackman Capital Partners’ 888 N. Douglas property in El Segundo. The space will serve as the company’s U.S. headquarters and represents a relocation from 50,000 square feet of space in Huntington Beach. The tenant will move into its new space after construction concludes in 2027. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham, and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean USA in the new lease. Hackman Capital represented itself. “This is a transformative change for Innocean USA, and we spent years advising the leadership team to help find a ‘one of one’ facility that would bring their company vision of the future to reality,” said Fine. “This is going to be a special place where their employees and creativity will absolutely thrive.”  Across from the Lakers’ practice facility and the L.A. Times headquarters, 888 Douglas is a 30-acre campus with four buildings totaling approximately 550,000 square feet. Hackman Capital purchased the 1930s-era aerospace manufacturing site in 2016 and invested $100 million to transform it into a creative office campus. Image courtesy of Gensler. The post Innocean USA Signs 100K-SF lease with Hackman Capital in Headquarters Relocation appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Innocean USA (ad agency) signs 101K SF HQ at Hackman Capital's 888 Douglas, El Segundo
Nearly doubles footprint from 50K SF in Huntington Beach; move-in 2027
Major employer relocation to LAX-adjacent office campus; ~600 employee base
stories.summary: Advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, California. The company is relocating nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach, with occupancy in 2027. The space includes a production facility for commercials and content.
stories.impact: Employer relocation to LAX-adjacent El Segundo signals job-base growth and demographic in-migration into the South Bay/LAX corridor, a historically underserved multifamily market. Nearly 600 relocated white-collar workers and supply-chain effects (contractors, vendors, service workers) will drive incremental rental demand in walkable multifamily near El Segundo and nearby LAX Gateway submarket. Developers should scout land/development sites within 3–5 miles for Class A and workforce housing to capture the wage-earner inflow.

stories.title: MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial
stories.excerpt: Ariel Property Advisors closed the sale of 425 Devoe Ave., a vacant multi-story industrial property in the West Farms neighborhood of The Bronx, for $10,750,000. The property spans 60,000 square feet above grade, which translates to $180 per square foot, with an additional 30,000 square feet below grade. An Ariel investment sales team led by senior director Jason M. Gold, along with partner Sean R. Kelly, Esq. and director Daniel Mahfa represented the seller, Abingdon Square Partners. The buyer was MADDD Equities, LLC. “The sale of 425 Devoe Ave. demonstrates the strong demand for large, commercial sites offering convenient regional access,” said Gold. Situated on a 40,097-square-foot lot, the property features four levels of usable industrial and warehouse space. It is located near the 2 and 5 subway lines and offers convenient access to the Cross Bronx Expressway, Sheridan Boulevard and the broader New York region. The post MADDD Equities Scoops Up Vacant West Farms Industrial appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: MADDD Equities acquires vacant West Farms industrial (60K SF above-grade) for $10.75M
425 Devoe Ave., Bronx; $180/SF; near 2/5 subway and Cross Bronx Expressway
Strong demand for large commercial sites with regional access signals industrial-to-residential conversion potential
stories.summary: MADDD Equities closed the acquisition of 425 Devoe Avenue, a vacant 60,000-square-foot (above-grade) multi-story industrial property in the Bronx's West Farms neighborhood, for $10.75 million ($180/SF). The 40,097-square-foot lot includes 30,000 SF below-grade space and is well-positioned near subway access and regional highways.
stories.impact: Underutilized industrial assets in transit-rich Bronx submarkets are increasingly acquisition targets for adaptive reuse or redevelopment. Buyer acquisition at this price point and site characteristics (size, transit, highway access) suggest conversion feasibility into mixed-use residential or workforce/affordable housing. Developers should monitor West Farms, Mott Haven, and similar Bronx industrial corridors for land-cost advantages and zoning-conversion opportunities as industrial-to-residential arbitrage widens.

stories.title: Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development
stories.excerpt: Shopoff Realty Investments has secured unanimous approval from the Buena Park City Council for 5600 Beach Blvd, a 13.76-acre residential development in Buena Park. The property is currently occupied by the Amway Corporation with a corporate sale-leaseback in place until the end of 2026 and consists of two industrial buildings totaling approximately 370,031 square feet. “5600 Beach Blvd represents an important step forward for Orange County and is intended to help address the need for attainable and diverse housing options for first-time homebuyers and for Buena Park’s growing senior population,” said Shopoff Realty Investments’ president and CEO, Bill Shopoff. “Transforming an industrial site into a vibrant residential community aligns with the city and county’s evolving needs, providing homes for people at every stage of life.” The development aims to deliver 231 three-story townhomes and duplex units, offered with four different floor plans, along with 50 for-rent senior affordable housing units. Homes are expected to be delivered in 2029-2030. Where the apartment industry connects. Meet the owners, investors, developers, lenders, brokers, and service providers driving today’s multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Build relationships, uncover opportunities, and stay ahead of what’s next. The post Shopoff Secures Approval for Buena Park Residential Development appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Shopoff Realty secured unanimous Buena Park City Council approval for 5600 Beach Blvd residential
13.76-acre Amway corporate site conversion; 231 townhomes + 50 senior affordable units; delivery 2029–2030
Industrial-to-residential pivot addresses first-time homebuyer and senior housing demand in Orange County
stories.summary: Shopoff Realty Investments received unanimous approval from Buena Park City Council for a 13.76-acre residential development at 5600 Beach Blvd. The project converts a former Amway corporate industrial site (370,031 SF, sale-leaseback expires end-2026) into 231 townhomes/duplexes and 50 for-rent senior affordable units across four floor plans. Delivery is expected in 2029–2030.
stories.impact: Successful entitlement and industrial-to-residential conversion in Orange County signals demand for attainable housing and municipal appetite for alternative uses on industrial land. However, this is for-sale and rental-senior product, not core multifamily apartments. Secondary signal: Amway's early lease exit suggests corporate footprint rationalization in OC, reducing light-industrial employment base but opening land opportunities. Monitor similar OC industrial leases and corporate departures for land acquisition windows.

stories.title: Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M
stories.excerpt: Marcus & Millichap completed the sale of Park Plaza, a retail center in Matawan, NJ. The asset sold for $14.67 million. “Park Plaza attracted significant investor interest due to its diverse tenant mix, strong visibility and strategic location within one of Monmouth County’s most established retail corridors,” said Seth Goldberg, associate director investments in Marcus & Millichap’s New Jersey office. “Well-positioned neighborhood shopping centers with durable cash flow continue to be highly sought after, and this transaction reflects the sustained demand for quality retail assets in New Jersey.” Goldberg, Brent Hyldahl and Alan Cafiero of Marcus & Millichap marketed the property for the seller and procured the buyer, both private investors from New Jersey. Located at 343-351 State Rte. 34, the retail center sits on a 5.86-acre lot totaling 61,750 square feet. It was built in 1986 and contains 20 suites. The rent roll features a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail and service-oriented tenants, including a Dunkin’ with a drive-thru. The post Matawan Retail Trades to Private Investor for $15M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Park Plaza retail center, Matawan NJ, trades for $14.67M; 61,750 SF, 20 suites, built 1986
5.86-acre lot; durable tenant mix (Dunkin', dining, services) on Route 34 corridor
Strong investor demand for neighborhood retail with stable cash flow despite broader retail disruption
stories.summary: Marcus & Millichap closed the sale of Park Plaza, a 61,750-square-foot retail center in Matawan, NJ, for $14.67 million. The 5.86-acre property, built in 1986, houses 20 tenant suites with a diverse mix of dining, lifestyle, retail, and service tenants anchored by a Dunkin'. Both buyer and seller are private NJ investors.
stories.impact: Minimal relevance to multifamily development. Neighborhood retail transactions reflect commercial real estate activity, not residential demand or supply signals. No secondary effects on apartment fundamentals or land availability in this transaction.

stories.title: Longfellow Sells Hatch Life Sciences Building in LIC for $87M
stories.excerpt: Life sciences developer Longfellow Real Estate Partners has parted with its first-ever New York City project at a discount. Longfellow’s Hatch Life Sciences Building, located at 43-10 23 Street in Long Island City, Queens, has sold for $86.9 million, according to city records filed Friday. Pearl Realty Management’s Jack Guttman signed for the buyer, under the entity 4310 23 St. A representative of Pearl Realty Management did not respond to requests for comment. Longfellow purchased the existing building at 43-10 23 Street in 2021 alongside its partner, Steven Orbuch’s Sculptor Real Estate, for $92.5 million. Longfellow, led by CEO and co-founder Adam Sichol, planned to invest another $120 million into turning the former parachute manufacturing plant into a mix of life sciences labs and offices. Construction had all but wrapped up when Commercial Observer visited in 2024. The final product spanned over 208,000 square feet across seven floors, including prebuilt lab suites, modular research space and flexible office areas. Longfellow and Sculptor did not respond immediately to requests for comment on the sale. While Guttman’s plans for the purchase remain unclear, the landlord appears to be active in the Long Island City market. Recent purchases include the Standard Motors Product Building at 37-18 Northern Boulevard for $42 million and BrightSpire Capital‘s office building at 21-02 49th Avenue for $28 million. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Longfellow Real Estate sells Hatch Life Sciences Building (LIC, Queens) for $86.9M
Purchased 2021 for $92.5M + $120M capex; 208K SF, 7 floors; life sciences/office labs
Loss-adjusted sale signals life sciences lab market softening or capital-constraint in specialized asset class
stories.summary: Longfellow Real Estate Partners sold its Hatch Life Sciences Building at 43-10 23rd Street in Long Island City, Queens, for $86.9 million. Longfellow had acquired the former parachute manufacturing plant in 2021 for $92.5 million and invested $120 million in conversion to 208,000 SF of lab suites, modular research space, and flexible office. The sale to Pearl Realty Management reflects a loss relative to total basis.
stories.impact: Life sciences build-to-suit capital intensity and potential oversupply or demand softening in Queens is a cautionary signal. However, minimal direct impact on multifamily unless LIC's life sciences boom (biotech, pharma) was a co-driver of residential demand; if so, slower lab space absorption may slow ancillary residential absorption in LIC. Developers active in Queens/LIC should monitor life sciences leasing velocity and tenant credit quality to gauge sustained job-base and wage-earner demand in the submarket.

stories.title: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Buys Two Miami Affordable Housing Rentals
stories.excerpt: Barry Sternlicht’s Starwood Asset Management has acquired two affordable housing properties in Miami-Dade County from the Gatehouse Group, paying a combined $63.8 million, property records show. In the largest deal, the investor paid $34 million for the 150-unit Magnolia Landing Apartments in the Naranja neighborhood, near the southern end of the county. Built in 2011, the 4.8-acre asset houses 20 three-story buildings at 25881 Southwest 143rd Court, just west of the South Dixie Highway. The sale breaks down to roughly $226,660 per unit. CBRE Capital Partners provided a $23.8 million Freddie Mac loan. Across the county in Miami’s Little River neighborhood, Starwood paid $29.75 million for the 160-unit Lafayette Square complex. The 19-story building sits on a 1.2-acre site, a block west from Northeast Second Avenue at 150 Northeast 79th Street. The deal equates to about $185,900 per apartment. The Gatehouse Group appears to have retained ownership of the adjacent 136-unit property. The Mansfield, Mass.-based firm developed both the Lafayette Square and Magnolia Landing Apartments, completing the former in 2008 and the latter in 2011. Representatives for Starwood and Gatehouse Group did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Starwood Asset Management (Barry Sternlicht) buys two Miami-Dade affordable properties; $63.8M combined
Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja) $34M; Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River) $29.75M
Institutional capital targeting affordable rentals in Miami-Dade; Freddie Mac financing support
stories.summary: Starwood Asset Management acquired two affordable rental properties in Miami-Dade County from Gatehouse Group for combined $63.8 million. Magnolia Landing (150 units, Naranja, $34M or $226.7K/unit) consists of 20 three-story buildings built in 2011. Lafayette Square (160 units, Little River, $29.75M or $185.9K/unit) is a 19-story building. CBRE Capital Partners secured a $23.8M Freddie Mac loan for Magnolia.
stories.impact: Starwood's institutional-scale acquisition of older affordable stock in Miami-Dade signals recognition of supply scarcity, rent growth, and resident income constraints in a high-cost gateway. This caps market pricing power for new affordable development and indicates that secondary-market acquisitions of 2010s-era affordable assets offer better risk-adjusted returns than new construction in saturated markets. For TCR, this suggests Miami-Dade affordable rents are rising fast enough to justify repositioning or new development, but also that seasoned-asset competition will intensify; focus on land and entitlements now to beat the capital flood.

stories.title: Ad Agency Doubles Office HQ Space in Move to Hackman Campus in L.A.
stories.excerpt: An international advertising agency is more than doubling its office footprint with a new headquarters lease in El Segundo, Calif. Innocean USA signed the 101,000-square-foot deal at Hackman Capital Partners’ creative office campus in the small enclave just south of Los Angeles International Airport. The agency will relocate nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach after construction on its new space concludes in 2027, according to JLL, which represented the tenant. The company reportedly will use part of the space as a production facility for commercials and other content. Terms of the lease were not disclosed. “This move is about creating the right environment for our next chapter,” Innocean USA CEO Steve Jun said in a statement. “This is an investment in our people, our clients, and the future we’re building together.” The complex, named after its address at 888 Douglas Street, includes four buildings totaling 550,000 square feet over 30 acres. Hackman acquired the former Northrop Grumman aerospace manufacturing complex in 2016, and invested about $100 million converting it into the creative office. Other major occupiers at the property have included L’Oréal USA, which signed for more than 100,000 square feet in 2021, and Beyond Meat, which originally leased 280,000 square feet for its headquarters. Aerospace and defense companies have also returned to L.A.’s South Bay, and helped bolster leasing at the El Segundo campus. Hypersonic aircraft developer Hermeus signed for 62,552 square feet earlier this year, while Varda Space Industries expanded to 54,749 square feet in 2025. Innocean USA is the U.S. arm of Innocean Worldwide, which was created by Hyundai Motor Group. JLL’s Jason Fine, Jeff Ingham and Mitch Lundquist represented Innocean, while Hackman was represented in-house. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Innocean USA doubles office footprint: 101K SF HQ at Hackman Capital's 888 Douglas, El Segundo
Relocates ~600 employees from 50K SF Huntington Beach; occupancy 2027; production facility included
Major ad-agency employer expansion in LAX-adjacent South Bay corridor
stories.summary: International advertising agency Innocean USA signed a 101,000-square-foot headquarters lease at Hackman Capital Partners' 888 Douglas creative office campus in El Segundo, California. The company is relocating nearly 600 employees from 50,000 square feet in Huntington Beach, more than doubling its footprint. Occupancy is slated for 2027, and the space includes a production facility for commercials and content creation.
stories.impact: Employer expansion and headquarters relocation to LAX-adjacent El Segundo signals sustained job-base growth and inbound migration of ~600 white-collar workers into the South Bay corridor. Indirect demand for rental housing in proximity to El Segundo and LAX Gateway submarket will accelerate; service and supply-chain workers will follow. Developers should prioritize land acquisition and feasibility studies for Class A and workforce multifamily product within 2–5 miles of 888 Douglas to capture wage-earner and household in-migration; timing aligns with 2027 occupancy ramp-up and job placement cycles.
